title: Introduction to Async Redux
overview: Async operations in Redux are used when the application needs to perform tasks that take time, such as API calls, file operations, or database requests.

example.title: Async Flow
example.content:
Component
 ↓
Async Request
 ↓
API Response
 ↓
Update Store

title: Why Async Handling is Needed
overview: Redux reducers are synchronous, so asynchronous operations need middleware to handle delayed responses.

example.title: Sync vs Async
example.content:
Synchronous:
Action → Reducer → State

Asynchronous:
Action → Middleware → API → Reducer → State

title: Redux Thunk
overview: Redux Thunk is middleware that allows action creators to return functions instead of only objects, making API calls possible.

example.title: Thunk Example

title: createAsyncThunk
overview: Redux Toolkit provides createAsyncThunk to simplify handling API requests with pending, fulfilled, and rejected states.

example.title: createAsyncThunk Example

title: Handling Loading and Error States
overview: Async operations should manage loading, success, and error states to provide a better user experience.

title: API Data Flow with Redux
overview: Redux stores API data globally so multiple components can access the same data without repeated requests.

example.title: API Flow
example.content:
Component
 ↓
dispatch(fetchData())
 ↓
API Call
 ↓
Slice Update
 ↓
UI Update

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how Redux handles asynchronous operations using middleware, Redux Thunk, createAsyncThunk, and API state management.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Redux is synchronous by default.
✔ Middleware handles async work.
✔ createAsyncThunk manages API calls.
✔ Loading and errors should be handled.
